body:
`parse()` compiles its regexes with `re.IGNORECASE`, so lowercase `am`, `pm` and `z` match the datetime patterns — but `date_convert()` then compares them case-sensitively.

Two consequences today:

```python
parse('{:tt}', '03:00 pm')[0]  # datetime.time(3, 0)      — silently wrong, should be 15:00
parse('{:tt}', '12:30 am')[0]  # datetime.time(12, 30)    — should be 00:30
parse('{:ti}', '2023-01-15T10:30:00z')
# ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''  — 'z' misses the
# `if tz == "Z"` branch and falls into the numeric-offset parser
```

The fix normalises the captured meridiem with `.upper()` after stripping, and recognises the Zulu marker case-insensitively. Tests added next to the existing `{:tt}` cases in `test_datetimes` (fail before, pass after; full suite `102 passed, 1 skipped`).

<sub>AI-assisted contribution (fix authored with an AI coding agent, verified by the human submitter).</sub>
